messages.body_plain:
I had posted this issue on GitHub as well, and the problem was  due to a bug in the software when using the QMC=TRUE option, and  is now fixed.  From Phil Chalmers:

"Thanks very much for the report. This was indeed an implementation bug when using QMC integration post-convergence. For whatever reason I forgot to include the latent mean/variable shift in the integration grid after the models were fitted, and M2() was one such area where this makes a large difference. I've added this into the package now to fix the problem, which also appeared in fscores() and residuals(). Quite frustrating, but I'm glad this was detected."

More detail on the problem and fix can be found in the now closed issue on the mirt Github respository:
https://github.com/philchalmers/mirt/issues/240

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I want to create a 2PL model for an MCQ item test. The data contains 82 item columns and 192 rows, with 0 OR 1 responses. I used ltm package in R. This was the code:

IRT_nonword_model <- ltm(IRT_nonword_df ~ z1, IRT.param = TRUE,
                         control = list(GHk = 20, iter.em = 20))

However, I kept getting error messages before and after I added the control. This is the error message:

"Error in solve.default(object$hessian) : system is computationally singular: reciprocal condition number = 3.87811e-21"

Admittedly the dataset contains a lot of 0 compared to 1 because the items are pseudowords that were included in the test to penalize guessing.

Could you please suggest a way to overcome this issue?

I would appreciate your help a lot!

Many thanks,
Alaa

Hi Deon de Bruin,

The GGUM is rather sensitive to starting values, so sometimes it makes sense to try a handful of random starts to see if they converge to the same solution. When I run your code with mirt(..., GenRandomPars = TRUE) the model seems to converge to something closer to the GPCM competitor. Phil

On Wed, Jun 14, 2023 at 8:00 AM Deon de Bruin <deond...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Dear colleagues
>
> I hope you will be able to shed light on some unusual results we obtained when fitting the generalized graded unfolding model (GGUM). In our example we have six items (scored on a three-point rating scale: 0 to 2). We first fitted the generalized partial credit model (GPCM) and the GGUM with mirt to five items (omitting the second item). We also fitted the GGUM with Tendeiro’s GGUM package.
>
> The mirt GGUM analysis did not properly converge after 500 iterations, but the max-change was relatively small.
>
> Iteration: 500, Log-Lik: -6565.962, Max-Change: 0.00031
>
> EM cycles terminated after 500 iterations.
>
>
>
> The correlations between the thetas were as follows:
>
> mirt.GPCM and mirt.GGUM: 0.999
>
> mirt.GGUM and Tendeiro.GGUM: 0.999
>
> mirt.GPCM and Tendeiro.GGUM: 0.999
>
> These results did not suggest an unfolding process.
>
>
> Adding a single item (labelled Item3) yielded the following correlations between the thetas:
>
> mirt.GPCM and mirt.GGUM: 0.125
>
> mirt.GGUM and Tendeiro.GGUM: 0.007
>
> mirt.GPCM and Tendeiro.GGUM: 0.999
>
> The thetas yielded by the mirt and Tendeiro GGUM packages now were very different and this appears to be the result of including a single item. Whereas the mirt GGUM analysis suggests an unfolding process, the Tendeiro GGUM analysis does not.
>
> It is possible that we might be overlooking something or making an error in specifying the ggum analysis in mirt. We include our R script (below) and the data with this message. We will appreciate it very much if you could comment or advise with respect to our results. In particular we hope to understand better why the results of the GGUM analyses with the two packages first are almost identical, and then dramatically different (when an extra item is added).
>
> Deon de Bruin
>
>
> ###########
>
> library(psych)
>
> dat <- read.csv(file.choose())
>

>

> cor(mirt.gpcm.theta, Tendeiro.ggum.theta[, 2], use = "complete.obs")
> cor(mirt.ggum.theta, Tendeiro.ggum.theta[, 2], use = "complete.obs")
>

> plot(Tendeiro.ggum.theta[, 2], mirt.ggum.theta,

> plot(Tendeiro.ggum.theta[, 2], mirt.gpcm.theta,

> plot(mirt.ggum.theta, mirt.gpcm.theta,

messages.body_plain:
Dear Colleagues,
We were conducting DIF analysis using the mirt package and ran into an issue where we got different results (1) when running DIF() to assess DIF sweeping through all items and (2) when analyzing item-by-item manually using multipleGroup().

The DIF() sweep returns results with large AIC and SABIC changes for all items, which seems unusual. So we did some spot checks and the manual check showed little changes in AIC and BIC for the two items we checked. I thought the results from the sweep and manual analyses should be the same. So I hope to be able to get some insights from you.

Thank you for your help in advance!
Best,
Shuting

Here is our code for DIF testing. I also attached the files to reproduce the results.
########
library(tidyverse)
library(mirt)

useData <- readRDS("./comboDat.RDS")

# comment out line 20 and uncomment line 24 if you do not want to re-run the DIF-sweep that takes several hours!

set.seed(9644)
mirtCluster(4)
fit_sex_mod1 <- multipleGroup(data=useData[which(!is.na <http://is.na>(useData$useChildSex)),str_detect(colnames(useData), "v3d")],
                              model=1,
                              group=as.factor(useData$useChildSex[which(!is.na <http://is.na>(useData$useChildSex))]),
                              itemtype="graded",
                              invariance=c("free_means","free_vars","slopes","intercepts"),
                              method="MHRM",
                              SE=TRUE,
                              SE.type="MHRM",
                              technical=list(NCYCLES=5000, BURNIN=200, SEMCYCLES=150),
                              verbose=TRUE)
dropSex <- DIF(fit_sex_mod1, which.par=c("a1","d1","d2","d3"), scheme="drop", p.adjust='fdr') # note this runs for several hours

mirtCluster(remove = TRUE)

# dropSex <- readRDS("./dropSex.RDS") # in case you don't want to run that on its own!

dropSex # everything is highly significant

# but test just one item - spot-check examples

#spot check Item v3d001
testv3d001 <- multipleGroup(data=useData[which(!is.na <http://is.na>(useData$useChildSex)),str_detect(colnames(useData), "v3d")],
                            model=1,
                            group=as.factor(useData$useChildSex[which(!is.na <http://is.na>(useData$useChildSex))]),
                            itemtype="graded",
                            invariance=c("free_means","free_vars",
                                         colnames(useData)[which(str_detect(colnames(useData), "v3d") &
                                                                   colnames(useData) != "v3d001")]),
                            method="MHRM",
                            SE=TRUE,
                            SE.type="MHRM",
                            technical=list(NCYCLES=5000, BURNIN=200, SEMCYCLES=150),
                            verbose=TRUE)

anova(fit_sex_mod1, testv3d001) # delta-AIC is about 16, delta-BIC is about -7, but DIF sweep suggests diff is around -2400

# spot check v3d092

testv3d092 <- multipleGroup(data=useData[which(!is.na <http://is.na>(useData$useChildSex)),str_detect(colnames(useData), "v3d")],
                            model=1,
                            group=as.factor(useData$useChildSex[which(!is.na <http://is.na>(useData$useChildSex))]),
                            itemtype="graded",
                            invariance=c("free_means","free_vars",
                                         colnames(useData)[which(str_detect(colnames(useData), "v3d") &
                                                                   colnames(useData) != "v3d092")]),
                            method="MHRM",
                            SE=TRUE,
                            SE.type="MHRM",
                            technical=list(NCYCLES=5000, BURNIN=200, SEMCYCLES=150),
                            verbose=TRUE)

anova(fit_sex_mod1, testv3d092)
